body: claimed: Codex (len) · 2026-11-22 19:01:08 UTC · branch mkinney:issue/3548-ui-lib-segfault · plan: Reproduce the UI GPU probe crash and pin the smallest fix.

Looks already fixed on upstream/main 6e641dac7: gpu_probe_and_headless_render_survive_parallel_start passes without a production change. Suggest closing; the maintainer decides.

The local pin runs the adapter probe and the headless renderer together eight times. It passed in 3.01 seconds. The test command was:

`cargo xtask gate test gpu_probe_and_headless_render_survive_parallel_start --crate camcraft-ui --exact`

This local result does not prove that the intermittent crash on uma is fixed. I did not run the pin on uma. No known fixing commit was found.

The failed artifact shows that adapter_probe_names_the_gpu passed before the crash. It contains graphics-device permission warnings. It contains no backtrace or core file. The crashing test remains unknown.

The same UI library SIGSEGV was reported in #2807 before PR #3363. The GPU seam merge does not establish the cause.

STOPPED because the pin passes on unchanged production code. No production code changed. No PR was opened. Claim released.

Coordinator: this issue stays open for now. A pass on one machine does not show that the fault is gone.

- The crash was seen one time, on the runner `uma`, at commit 87fb95f29. No run of `uma` after that commit has completed the step `ui suites: lib` yet (the later green runs were on `wopr-2` and `cheese`).
- No commit between 87fb95f29 and 6e641dac7 changes `crates/ui` or `crates/gpu` start code, so "already fixed on main" has no change that explains it.
- The new pin (`gpu_probe_and_headless_render_survive_parallel_start`) is a good test. A PR that adds it is welcome, with `Refs` to this issue.

Close condition: three green runs of `ui suites: lib` on `uma` after 87fb95f29, or a found cause. I record each run of `uma` here. If the crash comes again, the core dump of the runner is the next step.

The crash is seen on Windows also. This is no more a fault of one Linux runner.

Local run, 2026-11-22, Windows, a trial tree of `main` 6e641dac7 with three PRs merged (#3487, #3157, #3160): the step `ui suites: lib` ended with `0xc0000005 STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION` 5 seconds after the start, immediately after the line `running 1464 tests`, before a test result. Two more runs of the same binary were green (1456 passed, 8 ignored): one on the same tree, one on a tree with two of the PRs.

What the two sightings have in common:
- the ui lib test binary, with many test threads (16 on the runner, the default on Windows);
- the crash comes in the first seconds, with no test name and no panic text;
- the tree contains 87fb95f29 (the first commit in which `camcraft-ui` links `camcraft-gpu` and `wgpu`).

This points to a race at the start of the test binary (for example two tests that make a GPU adapter or a headless renderer at the same time), not to one test. The pin `gpu_probe_and_headless_render_survive_parallel_start` (eight parallel starts, green) did not find it; the real binary starts 1464 tests.

Next step for the worker: run the ui lib binary in a loop (for example 50 times) with the default threads to get the rate, then with `--test-threads=1` and with `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off`, and keep a crash dump of one failure. The close condition of the earlier comment does not apply any more: the fault is real.

claimed: issue-worker-high (Opus) · 2026-11-22 20:35 UTC · worktree/branch .claude/worktrees/issue-3442 issue/3548-ui-lib-start-crash · plan: get the crash rate of the ui lib binary in a loop, narrow it to the start code, fix at the cause or serialise the GPU start.

Not reproduced on Windows. The claim is released. No code changed, no branch was pushed and no PR was opened.

Tree: `origin/main` 5346bd7ac, debug `camcraft-ui` lib test binary (1477 tests), Windows 11, default thread count.

What I ran (exit code `0xc0000005` was the crash criterion):
- 1 full run: green, 1469 passed, 8 ignored, 92 s.
- 40 starts of the full binary, killed after 20 s each (the crash comes in the first 5 s): 0 crashes.
- 60 more starts of the full binary, as 4 copies at the same time, killed after 20 s: 0 crashes.
- 40 runs of the three GPU tests together, `--test-threads=16`: `headless_run_succeeds`, `a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window`, `adapter_probe_names_the_gpu`. 0 crashes.
- A temporary stress test (not committed): 16 threads, each makes and drops a `wgpu::Instance` with all native backends 10 times and enumerates the adapters. 5 runs, 0 crashes. With `request_device` on the first adapter too: 4 runs, 0 crashes, but each run took more than 300 s and was killed.
- Windows Error Reporting has no "Faulting module" entry for a camcraft binary on this machine.

Facts for the next worker:
- In the lib, only three tests that are not ignored make wgpu objects. Each test makes its own `wgpu::Instance`; no instance or device is shared:
  - `egui_app::tests::headless_run_succeeds`: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs:1094`, through `crates/gpu/src/adapter.rs:76`.
  - `egui_app::report_tests::a_kind_button_asks_the_shell_for_the_whole_window`: the screenshot command makes an `egui_kittest` `WgpuTestRenderer`. That renderer enumerates the adapters of all backends (Vulkan, DX12, GL).
  - `egui_app::gpu::tests::adapter_probe_names_the_gpu`: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/gpu.rs:223`.
- The #2807 comment of 2026-11-19 shows a Linux SIGSEGV in this binary right after `egui_app::report_tests::the_body_carries_the_questions_and_the_debug_report`. That module holds the one test that renders through kittest.
- Hypothesis (not proved): a race between instances of the wgpu GL backend (EGL on Linux) that are made or dropped on parallel test threads.

Recommended next step: get a core dump on the runner `uma` (`ulimit -c unlimited`), or a WER local dump on Windows (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\LocalDumps`). The faulting module decides between a wgpu or driver fault and our code. A blind lock around the three tests is possible, but without a reproduction no test can show that it removes the crash.
One data point: the gate job of the run of 16dc39f06 on the runner `uma` is green (22:51Z to 23:34Z), with `ui suites: lib`. No crash in that run.
